Mr. Khurshed Alam khan, Learned advocate appearing for the accused contemners at the very out set submits that the contemners by filing written statement supported by affidavit admitted their guilt and with sincere feeling of regret and penitence offered unqualified and unconditional apology and they have undertaken to be careful and not to repeat similar lapse in future and sought mercy of the Court. The learned Advocate further submits without having slightest intent at justifying the fault or latches being made in not submitting the compliance report the contemners feel obliged to bring pertinent fact to the kind notice of the learned court which is that the dealing officer was one O.S.I Fazlur Rahman who even though complied the order of this court by release and delivery of the house hold goods in question to accused petitioners on 07.03.2003 in time as ordered by the High Court Division submitted on compliance repot before the High Court Division with in stipulated time due to lack of understanding the meaning and purports of the English words, "submit report of compliance further within 1(one) week thereafter positively" and as such non reporting is an unintentional slip on the part of an officiating Sub Inspercor of Police for which cotemners beg apology. Mr. Khan had drawn our attention to the fact the reminders issued by the High Court Division on 19.03.2003 was received by the opposite party No 2 on 06.04.2003 and sent the same to O.C. Kafrul P.S. through D.C. (west) for taking necessary action and as such said Courts order by way of reminder was fully complied the attached goods were released but for negligence to duty and failure to submit compliance report to the High Court Division with in stipulate time departmental proceedings have already been started by the opposite Party No. 2 under the direction of the opposite party No. 3 against the delenquent officers and ministerial staffs. The learned advocate very humbly but emphatically submits that it is a fit a case where there being no culpable negligence or indifference to duty on the part to the accused contemners and the contemners having not violated or disobeyed order dated 09.02.2003 passed by the High Court Division knowingly, willfully or deliberately they deserve to be exonerated upon acceptance of apology offered by them Mr. Khan lastly made a grievance that news published by section of national dailies namely Dainik Pratham Alo, Sangbad and Jugantar regarding the charge of contempt faced by the top bass Police Officer Inspector General of Police and Policen like Commissioner before the High Court Division was exaggerated and press rendering of Dainik Pratham Alo was read out to us. When the learned advocate was informed by us that we found nothing unusual in the reporting the learned advocate no longer pressed the issue. 

 17. We have perused the connected records of the Criminal Misc. case No 6100 of 2002 the affidavit filed on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1-3 and the supplemantary affidavit filed on behalf of the opposite party No. 2 and heard the learned D.A.G and learned Additional Attorney General on behalf of the State and Mr. Khorshed Alam khan on behalf of the contemners opposite party Nos. 1-3 in extenso. 

 20. It is to be mentioned that in the meanwhile police Head Quarters issued police order No. 03-2003 dated 06.05.2003 in regard to compliance of courts order being is annexed as Annexure Z-21 to, the supplementary affidavit filed by the police Commissioner. This police order explicitly admits failure of the officer-in-charge Kafrul Police Station to comply with courts order dated 09.02.2003 in the back ground of the instant case. It speaks about the duty of the police to execute all lawful orders of the learned courts as provided under section 23 of the police act. The order itself had taken note of the fact that non compliance of any order of the court tantamount to contempt of court. The order issued by the police Head Quarters has expressed grave concern over the matter that due importance is not given and appropriate step for execution of courts order is not taken in time. As a result adverse impression is created against police sometime leading to initiation of contempt proceeding. This police order has also noted how in the present case officer-in-charge, Kafrul police station, Police Commissioner of DMP and Inspector General of Bangladesh police had to appear before the High Court Division personally before the court to account for the lapse. The order issued under the signature of the Inspector General of Bangladesh police and intended to be guideline for all units of the police force. Erects for taking necessary steps to ensure execution and enforcement of the orders issued by courts in all spheres as early as possible or within stipulated time to avoid undesirable situation as aforementioned failing which respective unit chief should have to stand accountable for any negligence or breach. 

 21. It appears the contemner opposite party No. 1 whom directed comply to with order of the High Court Division dated 09.02.2003 and subimt compliance report within one week of execution. After stipulated time for compliance expired and contempt rule was issued and served upon him the contemner came with an explanation dated 22.04.2003 stating that so-called original compliance report about the delivery of the goods to the owner concerned on 07.03.2003 after observing necessary formalities was communicated to the High Court Division under memo NO. 2114 dated 10.04.2003 and said original compliance was allegedly received by the High Court on 20.04.2003. But this statement regarding submission of so-called compliance report on 10.04.2003 and receipt thereof by the High Court Division on 20.04.2003 is not supported by any scrap of paper. The records of the original Criminal Misc. Case No, 6100 of 2002 or those of the instant Criminal Suo Motu Rule No. 4843 of 2003 nowhere bear any acknowledgment of receipt of such report on record. The contemner opposite party himself filed some papers along with affidavit filed on 24.04.2003 marked as Annexure-Z21 but no copy of the so called original compliance has been filed. It may be noted though photo copy of a report in Bangli under the signature of contemner opposite party dated 22.04.2003 captioned প্রতিবেদন 5ccitvi is available in the record of the original Criminal Misc. Case No. 6100 of 2002 it only referred to so called original report of compliance to the High Court Division bearing memo No. 2114 dated 10.04.2003. It appears photo copy of so called “বিষয় প্রতিবেদন”  with reference to Criminal Misc. case No. 6100 of 2002 reference No. 22689 dated 02.03.2003 bearing signature of the contemner opposite Party no. 1 dated 10.04.2003 addressed to Hon'ble Justice of the High Court Division as Annexure Ka and antothere photo copy of the same dated 11.04.2002 bearing signature of the opposite party No. 1 addressed to the Registrar of this court. There is nothing to show that the afforesaid two papers are formally entered into the records of the Rule File. These two bizarre material purporting to be so-called original compliance report are subsequently manipulated and inducted into record in connivance with biased interest employees of the Rule section.'  23. Under Section 23 of the police act (Act of 1861) police officer personnel is not only duty bound promptly to obey and execute a order issued passed by this court but also police officer found guilty of violation of dui or wilful breach of lawful order made by competent authority is liable to be punished provided under section 29 of the Act. It may be noted Bangladesh police is a discipline force as defined under Article 152 of the constitution. Pertinently it may be noted that under Article 112 of the constitution of the people Republic of Bangladesh all authorities executive and judicial in the Republic are enjoined to act in aid of the Supreme Court i implementing its decisions and order. Where High Court Division directed police for compliance of an order within a time frame is to be executed and enforced in full with the time and in the manner specified therein. The law enforcer in course of encorcement court's order should not put any artificial meaning or construction or execute any order partly half heartedly and haphazardly there or just as a matter of free choice, out of whir and caprice but promptly obey and enforce order strictly timely and in full that he required by such order to do. In case as difficulty arises in understanding the meaning and purport thereof concerned poll personnel is to seek guidance form I superior of the court which issued the order immediately. For failure to obey and complete with any order or direction passed by the High Court Division knowingly and deliberately concerned officer come under the mischief offence of contempt of court with in the meaning of section 3 of the contempt of court's Act, 1926 (XII of 1926) and he is liable to be committed and punished under the said Act. 

 24. In the instant case we directed particular police officer namely the officer-in-charge, Kafrul police station to obey and enforce our order dated 09.02.2003 and submit a report of compliance within stipulated time and by such order a duty is cast upon said officer-in-charge, Kafrul police station to promptly obey and execute the order and submit or compliance report within stipulated time wherein he had admittedly failed. 

 26. On going through the order dated 09.02.2003 and subsequent orders dated 12.03.2003, 19.03.2003 and order dated 12.04.2003 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. Case No. 6100 of 2002 and the facts and circumstances disclosed in the affidavits filed by the contemners opposite party No. 2 Police Commissioner read with compliance report order dated 22.04.2003 submitted by the contemner opposite party no. 1 we are unable to accept the explanation that O.S.  28. In view of the above we find contemners opposite parties no 1 having not obeyed and complied with aforesaid lawful order dated 09.02.2003 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. Case No. 6100 of 2002 within stipulated time knowingly, willfully and purposely with a view to undermining the authority of the court and thereby impeding and obstructing the free flow of justice as guilty of contempt of the High Court Division in gross form and deserves to the punished severely with maximum sentence provided under the law. 

 31. It appears the accused contemners, Police commissioner and inspector General of police offered then respective apology at the first available opportunity by filing written statement supported by affidavit. We find that the police commissioner and the Inspector of General Police were not included in the original order dated 09.02.2003 and initially they did not have any liability regarding compliance thereof; they came in the scene when they were directed to secure compliance of our order by a reminder issued from this court on 19.03.2003. We find from the record that by order dated 09.02.2003 we directed the officer-in-charge, Kafrul police station to enforce the order and submit a compliance report. It is correctly stated that contemner opposite party No. 2 received reminder of this court on 06.04.2003 and he immediately sent to the officer-in-charge of Kafrul police station for compliance. The Inspector General of police openly and frankly stated that as the reminder order dated 19.03.2003 was not placed before him for which it was no possible for him to issue the departmental instruction or directive to the units regarding compliance of courts order on priority basis or with in stipulated time. But contemner opposite party No. 2 as the former Inspector General of police possessed full authority and control to supervise the activities of the subordinate units under him and was competent to issue such departmental circular or order as of routine. It appears that the successor Inspector General of police, Bangladesh Police issued necessary Police order bearing No. 03/2003 dated 06.05.2003 wherein the police force units under him have been directed to take necessary steps to ensure enforcement of orders of courts at all spheres at the earliest or with in stipulated time under respective individual supervision of unit chiefs to avoid any undesirable situation as in the instant case and for any negligence or latches the unit chief held responsible. It seems the contemners conferred unconditional and unreserved apology admitting their guilt and they have not only expressed sincere regret and penitence for the unintentional error but they have undertaken not to repeat similar mistake in future. The contemners appear to be genuinely sorry and penitent for the lapse done we are also told Dr. Mohammad Ali, who represented Accused Md. Akram Khan Misc. Case No. 6100/2002 that his client had already received the attached house hold goods from Kafrul P.S. Custody on 07.03.2003,

Abdul Quayyum and Inspector General of police Modabbir Hossain Chowdhury be and they are hereby exonerated from the instant contempt proceedings with the admonition that they failed to exercise supervisory authority and control over their subordinates in obtaining timely compliance of courts order dated 09.02.2003 in Criminal Misc. Case No. 6100/2002.
